estimate: Insurance premium (four companies with no premium figure; Keystone uses its own $285,000)
method: Median of the five portfolio companies that state a 2025 premium, as a share of LTM revenue, times the US casualty rate change, applied to the whole premium as an upper bound
input: 0.29% of revenue (range 0.13% to 1.44%, n=5); casualty rate +7% (Marsh, Q2 2026)
cross_check: RIMS total cost of risk is 1.0% of revenue, 3.4 times the portfolio median
result: consistent as an upper bound only
reading: The RIMS figure includes retained losses and administration, so it overstates the premium; the observed portfolio ratio is used and RIMS is kept as the ceiling.

estimate: Supplier concentration (eight companies without a supplier file)
method: McKinsey Global Institute: more than 40% of a year's profit lost per decade over a disruption every 3.7 years, scaled by a dependence factor of 0.25 (people and facility services) or 0.5 (equipment and consumables)
input: 14.8% of one year's EBITDA per disruption before scaling; resulting impacts 3.7% to 7.4% of EBITDA
cross_check: Company-specific sole-source impacts from supplier files: sterling 15.2% of EBITDA; harvest 18.1% of EBITDA
reading: The two goods makers with their own supplier files sit at 15 to 18% of EBITDA per disruption, at or just above the 14.8% benchmark. Both are Kith's own one-lead-time calculation, so this is a consistency check, not independent evidence; the service companies are scaled down by judgment, so confidence is low.
